**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The licence grant in §§ 13.1–13.3 sits at the **preferred** position on every material term of the LICENSE rule:

- **Affiliates and contractors:** § 13.1 grants access rights directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" — no written-notice or consent gate, so better than the fallback.
- **Perpetual/irrevocable for paid-up:** § 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence," including modification, derivative works, and contractor support.
- **No revocation at will:** § 13.3 permits revocation or suspension only during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — nowhere near walk-away territory.
- **Transferability:** § 13.3 allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor under a § 24-permitted assignment, and § 24.1 lets Customer assign to an M&A successor without Vendor consent.

Noted but not flagged: § 14.2's "revocable, non-transferable" Deliverable licence limited to the Order Form term creates tension, though § 14.3 imports the § 13.2 perpetual licence for Vendor Technology in Deliverables. That is a Deliverable ownership/IP issue and should be raised under the IP rule rather than double-flagged here.
